@@info: Keys that exist in <en> but not in <ru>.
The values below are the en source text — replace them with ru translations.
You do not have to translate all of them; leave out what you are unsure about and open a PR.
A maintainer then runs 'npm run i18n:apply' to merge this file into messages/ru.json.
Anything still missing afterwards simply renders in en at runtime.
Plurals — ru uses the forms: one, few, many, other. "other" is required.
(add "plural": "total" to count another input instead of {count}).
Inside a sentence, # is the number: "Read {count, plural, one {# band} other {# bands}}"
An exact number like "=0": "No bands" beats the forms above.
equalizer_player_file_decode_error: Couldn't play {name}. This browser may not support its audio format.
tutorial_eq_source_content: Switch the EQ on and pick the device to equalize. The result is drawn on the graph.
tutorial_eq_filters_content: Each row is a filter band. Set its frequency, gain and Q here, or drag its node on the graph.
tutorial_eq_constraint_hint: Making an EQ for a specific app or device? Pick it under Constraint, and the bands only take settings it accepts.
tutorial_eq_autoeq_content: Rather not tune by hand? AutoEQ fits the bands to a target for you.
tutorial_eq_listen_content: Hear the difference with the audio player, and keep earlier versions in History & Compare to A/B them.
tutorial_eq_bypass_hint: Tip: hold the backslash (\) key to flip the EQ on or off for a quick comparison.
tutorial_eq_hardware_content: Happy with it? Hardware EQ writes your bands straight to a supported device.
tutorial_eq_replay_hint: You can replay this tour anytime from the ? button at the top of this panel.
